about: How numbers are calculated. Each step cites a source line or an owner decision (C1-C8, taken in chat on 2026-10-08/09).

steps.text: Only the 10-digit mobile number is read. A leading +91, 91 or 0 is removed first. The number must start with 6, 7, 8 or 9.
Zero is skipped: 8-0-5 is read as 8-5, and 0 never goes on a grid.
Repeated digits only matter where a source says so (multiple 6 / multiple 7 on Venus-Ketu). A same-digit pair such as 9-9 has no meaning.
Two separate grids: the birth-date grid (all digits of DD MM YYYY, zeros skipped) and the mobile grid. Yogas are read on each. A planned number changes only the mobile grid.
On a yoga diagram, a red digit must be present, a red X must be absent, and a blank cell is ignored.
A 2- or 3-digit profession code matches when those digits are side by side in either order (19 or 91; 371 or 173). 'X AND Y' and single digits match anywhere in the number.

steps.quote: The speaker identifies a birth number of nine and a destiny number of three
steps.text: Birth number (mulank) = day of birth reduced to one digit. Destiny number (bhagyank) = all digits of the full date of birth added and reduced to one digit. Inferred from T01's example (18 September 2001 → birth 9, destiny 3).

steps.quote: add the day of birth, the month of birth, and the digits of the year being considered, reducing the result to a single digit
steps.text: Personal year = day + month + digit-sum of the year, reduced fully to one digit (11 → 2, 22 → 4). The calendar year is used: the story shows this year and next year.
Name number = sum of the Chaldean values of all letters in the name, reduced to one digit. No source gives the letter table, so the standard Chaldean table below is used; please confirm it.
